rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill with `name`/`description` front matter, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions`.

The requirement has two parts. The first is a MUST: the description states when to use the skill in terms of the user's task. The second is a MAY, which imposes nothing to check.

The `description` meets the MUST. It opens with "Use during design sessions and before changing code, tests, or requirement text in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas". It then covers requests such as a feature, bug fix, CLI flag, test, dependency bump or wording tweak, even when the user never says "requirement". It adds "Also use when writing or revising reference chapters". All of these are conditions on the user's task.

The description also names other bundled skills: "use habeas-refactor" and "use habeas-evidence". The MAY permits this, and it fits the case where an agent could confuse the skills. Adding a summary of what the skill does is not forbidden.

There are no listed violation matches to judge, and I found no gap.
